task: R07 - durable selection request, bounded device persistence and read-only cold restart recovery

productAuthority.rule: Pending Selection intent is retained and checked; another person cannot be selected while its outcome is unknown. Whole application identity and accepted terms remain immutable.

previousProblem.source: Candidates session useMemo initialized pending=null and no durable selection journal existed.
previousProblem.reproduction: Execute the actual pre-change choose callback with a lost HTTP response seam, then a fresh route session. The new route read the task and candidates but made zero receipt RPC calls and returned receipt=null.
previousProblem.evidenceLayer: local production callback execution with synthetic RPC transport; not a hosted write or Android process-kill test

implemented: One account/Need AsyncStorage record contains only version, accountId, needId and the seven original selection command fields.
New command is serialized, saved and read back before rpc_select_response. An identical existing durable record is read without another device write.
Failed, silent or unreadable storage cannot dispatch the business writer. Original request key is retained for recovery.
Fresh route/module restores command identity before current task or candidate reads. Recovery calls only rpc_read_selection_result.
NOT_FOUND retains the original command. A separate explicit resend reuses its original key, revision, application version/hash and people count.
A changed/unavailable offer uses the existing design primitives for a minimal recovery view without inventing old private offer/profile fields.
Every storage await checks the original account/focus/read generation. Logout, account change and A-to-B-to-A cannot authorize an old callback.
Only exact receipt or SQLSTATE-proven refusal permits identity retirement. Retirement is serialized and reads back actual absence; a late clear cannot erase a newer command.
A real receipt remains confirmed when local removal fails. The journal stays unresolved locally and blocks a different selection until removal succeeds.
Every journal operation has a five-second caller deadline starting at enqueue, so native get/set/remove and waiting behind another operation cannot leave the screen indefinitely loading.

The actual native promise remains in the per-account/Need serial chain after the caller deadline. A late remove must finish before a newer intent can be written; the timed race never releases that lock.

An operation-local authority predicate combines its active deadline with the original account/focus/read predicate. It is checked before native work and after every await; expired queued operations never start and late completions cannot continue readback or dispatch.
Elapsed wall-clock deadline is also checked in the predicate, so a delayed JS timer cannot authorize a native continuation after expiry.

Existing Candidates recovery and explicit-write callbacks return a proven server receipt with NOT_RETIRED_ON_DEVICE when local clear times out. Open Agreement remains available; no writer is invoked by a check, read timeout or storage timeout.

positiveScenarios: confirmed receipt and Open Agreement after hung local remove
successful explicit selection receipt after hung local cleanup
new intent waits for actual old native remove, then survives its late completion
queue recovers after expired native predecessor eventually finishes
negativeScenarios: another retained screen intent cannot be overwritten
failed/silent removal cannot enable a new choice
hung load get cannot restore a late command
hung save pre-read cannot reach set or writer
hung native set and saved-command readback cannot later dispatch
queued load/save/clear each expire from their own enqueue time without starting native work
expired operation and queued cleanup cannot regain authority after A-to-B-to-A
elapsed deadline before delayed timer callback cannot authorize continuation
receipt read timeout cannot resend an already checked command or adopt a late receipt
verification.harnessBoundary: Production TypeScript journal, reader, route callbacks and recovery presentation execute unchanged. AsyncStorage/RPC/account seams remain synthetic; timeout cases inject a controllable clock and scheduler only into the actual module loader. No Android bridge, real force-stop, native timing or hosted write is claimed.

server.contract: Existing rpc_read_selection_result and rpc_select_response are unchanged. Prior DEV/ordinary-Auth proof remains scripts/r07-selection-recovery-dev-20261107.receipt.json; it is not a new native persistence proof.

native.required: Install integrated QA APK, force-stop during and after selection, restart as original user, check read-only recovery, explicit replay, logout/account change and small-screen/large-text recovery.

limits: Does not reconstruct a previously lost memory-only pending selection from an older application version.
Cold restart assumes application storage remains intact; uninstall, clear-data and permanently corrupt device storage are not claimed recoverable.
A corrupt journal is retained and blocks new selection; it is not automatically discarded as proof that no server write happened.
No new source commit, GitHub CI, APK, DEV deployment or native acceptance is claimed by this local proof.
Three-actor last-place concurrency and all pricing variants remain separate verification scopes.

AsyncStorage cannot cancel a mutation already issued to native code. It may finish after caller timeout; the original immutable identity and serial chain prevent that completion from dispatching or overtaking a newer stored intent.

If the native promise never settles, operations for that same account/Need remain serialized and individually fail within their own five-second deadline. This patch does not claim repair of a permanently stalled device bridge; an application restart may be needed.
Five seconds bounds active-JS waiting. A suspended process cannot render or run timers; deadline and account/focus checks fence the next continuation on resume.
